_comment: Manual reviewer verdicts for the 076-f current-device assessment. Each entry is authored only after this reviewer opened the filed controller note AND the filed device frame and confirmed the row really shows that game. `identity` is the decisive field: a note describing a DIFFERENT game is never acceptance of the named game, no matter how good it looks. `status` uses only PASS / FIXED / NOT VALIDATED / N-A.

attention-odd-one-out.note: Controller note describes a 3x3 grid of triangles with one odd circle, Round 1/6, timer, Pause. Scored feedback quoted verbatim: "Time's up" with the odd one revealed. Pause overlay quotes "The challenge is hidden and the timers are frozen" with Resume/Quit; resume confirmed at Round 2/6. Result screen independently confirmed against the filed device frame item-for-item (Score 125, Accuracy 17%, First-try 17%, Rounds passed 1/6, Best streak 1, Timeouts 5, XP 12, Reward +12 XP +2 coins). Controls legible, Play again is the single red CTA, no clipping or overlap.

attention-sustained-vigilance.note: DOWNGRADED on review (finding F3). The note describes the right game and its mechanic (Tap GO / hold on the stop number, Trial 1/30) and it does quote the pause overlay ("Paused", "The challenge is hidden and the timers are frozen.", Resume/Quit, resume confirmed) and an itemised result (723, Go hits 2/26, Stop numbers held 4/4, Commissions 0, Mean reaction 743ms, Best streak 1, XP 27, +27 XP +5 coins). BUT section 2 quotes NO scored verdict: it only describes the feedback mechanism and claims feedback is continuous rather than an intermittent popup. That claim is factually wrong about the UI - attention-sustained-vigilance/components/stimulus-stage.tsx renders a per-trial verdict flash ("Go!", "Held - nice", "That was the stop number", "Missed one") with a ✓/✕/⏱ badge and a spoken verdict. Per the change spec feedback is not inferred, so scored feedback is NOT VALIDATED until a per-trial verdict is quoted from the device. FRAME CAVEAT (finding F4): the filed result.png/result.xml were captured after the journey exit step and show the HOME screen (home-brand, home-title, home-workout-cta, 0 of 4 complete), not any game state; they are not corroboration and are not cited as such.

attention-symbol-tracker.note: Controller note describes the tracking mechanic specifically: 3x3 grid of symbols with two highlighted symbol cards to memorize, "Track 2 symbols", "Memorize the highlighted symbols...", Round 1/5, Score 0, Pause. Scored feedback quoted: "Not quite", "You found 0 of 2 tracked symbols", "Time ran out - your picks were submitted as they stood."

attention-target-count.note: Covered by task 3.21 (its parent redesign task 6.4 was already checked, so this row is the fresh current-device check and does not inherit that check). Note opens with the identity line 'On-screen game title: Target Count'. All six states evidenced for the correct counting mechanic: active board is a shape grid with 'Count the star' / 'Count the diamond' instructions, Round 1/8, Score chip, Pause and five number-selection buttons; scored feedback QUOTED verbatim ('Time up' with reveal text such as 'There were 6 stars.'); pause overlay quoted ('Pause', 'Resume', 'Quit') with resume confirmed; result screen itemised (Keep training, Final score 0, Accuracy 0%, Rounds correct 0/8, Best streak 0, XP 10, Reward +10 XP +2 coins, Progress saved); taps immediate with safe exit and re-open; no defects observed. Counting mechanic retained.

flexibility-card-sort.note: RE-RUN after the first attempt was downgraded (findings F1/F2: no scored verdict, no pause/result, and a mis-filed frame belonging to attention-target-count). This run evidences the correct game decisively - the result-screen stats are card-sort's own layout (Accuracy, Speed, After rule switches, Discovery rounds, Best streak, Mistakes, XP), which no other game has. Active board: Round 1/10-10/10, score chips, Pause, rule banners 'Match by SHAPE' / 'Match by COLOR', 2x2 option-card grid. Scored feedback is now QUOTED (verdict 'Correct!' with descriptive match text 'Matched by shape: red circle') rather than the rule-switch notice that was wrongly quoted before. Pause overlay quoted ('Paused', 'The challenge is hidden and the timers are frozen.', Resume) with resume confirmed. Result screen itemised: 'Solid work', score 900, Accuracy 90%, Speed 0%, After rule switches 100%, Discovery rounds 67%, Best streak 5, Mistakes 1, XP 38, Reward +38 XP +7 coins, Progress saved. Taps immediate with safe exit and re-open; no defects observed. Sorting mechanic retained.

attention-visual-search.note: RE-RUN after the controller mis-navigated on the first attempt. This run's note opens with the identity line 'On-screen game title: Visual Search', which the tightened prompt requires before playing. All six states are evidenced for the correct game: active board is the odd-tile search board (2x2 grid expanding in later rounds, 'Find the odd tile', Round 1/12, Score, Pause, countdown timer); scored feedback is QUOTED verbatim ('Round failed' with subtitle 'Time's up - the odd tile was tile X' and the correct tile highlighted); pause overlay quoted ('Paused', 'The challenge is hidden and the timers are frozen.', Resume/Quit) with resume confirmed; result screen itemised (Score 0, Accuracy 0%, Rounds passed 0/4, Best streak 0, Avg response 0ms, Fastest response -, XP 10, Reward +10 XP +2 coins, Play again/Done); taps registered immediately with safe exit and re-open; no defects observed. Search mechanic retained.
